llm.reply:
Marfan syndrome is a multisystem connective tissue disorder with autosomal dominant inheritance, primarily caused by FBN1 gene mutation, that presents with diverse clinical manifestations across multiple organ systems [22: "Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance. It is mainly caused by FBN1 gene mutation and often has different clinical manifestations"]. Diagnosis relies on established criteria such as the Ghent II Nosology, which guides identification of high-risk patients, while management emphasizes early identification and intervention to improve prognosis [24: "The Ghent II Nosology of MFS criteria are crucial in MFS diagnosis, guiding clinicians in identifying high-risk patients"].

## Cardiovascular Features

Cardiovascular involvement represents a major disease manifestation. Aortic regurgitation is a documented clinical feature [7]. Congestive heart failure also occurs among affected individuals [28]. Clinical trials have specifically targeted aortic root pathology, including comparisons of medications aimed at slowing aortic root enlargement [8] and investigations of losartan therapy on aortic root dilation progression [20].

## Ocular Features

Ocular abnormalities are prominent in this condition. Ectopia lentis, a hallmark ocular finding, is listed among the clinical features [19]. Astigmatism is additionally recorded [15]. Strabismus manifestations include esotropia [23], exotropia [25], and hypertropia [29]. Glaucoma represents another recognized ocular complication [27].

## Musculoskeletal Features

Skeletal manifestations are characteristic and diagnostically relevant. Arachnodactyly, the distinctive long slender digits, is a documented feature [11]. Pes planus, or flatfoot deformity, is also associated with this syndrome [26]. Micrognathia, indicating abnormal mandibular development, appears among the recorded features [30].

Marfan syndrome is a multisystem connective tissue disorder with autosomal dominant inheritance caused mainly by FBN1 gene mutation, presenting with diverse clinical manifestations across multiple organ systems [22: "Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance. It is mainly caused by FBN1 gene mutation and often has different clinical manifestations"]. Diagnosis relies on the Ghent II Nosology criteria to identify high-risk patients, underscoring the importance of systematic screenings and close follow-ups [24: "The Ghent II Nosology of MFS criteria are crucial in MFS diagnosis, guiding clinicians in identifying high-risk patients"]. The literature encompasses review articles on latest advances in diagnosis and treatment [6], comprehensive clinical reviews [24], and educational overviews [10], alongside foundational studies [5][9][13][17][21] and ongoing clinical trials targeting aortic root disease progression [4][8][12][16][20].

## Cardiovascular Features

MedGen lists these clinical features: Aortic regurgitation [7], Congestive heart failure [28]. Cardiovascular involvement represents a major disease manifestation, with clinical trials specifically targeting aortic root enlargement through pharmacological interventions including losartan versus atenolol comparisons [16], ACE inhibitor therapy [12], and dedicated losartan therapy protocols [20].

## Ocular Features

MedGen lists these clinical features: Astigmatism [15], Ectopia lentis [19], Esotropia [23], Exotropia [25], Glaucoma [27], Hypertropia [29]. Ocular manifestations are diverse and well-documented in the MedGen clinical feature annotations, with ectopia lentis representing a hallmark diagnostic criterion in Ghent II Nosology.

## Musculoskeletal Features

MedGen lists these clinical features: Arachnodactyly [11], Pes planus [26], Micrognathia [30]. These skeletal manifestations contribute to the characteristic phenotype, with arachnodactyly serving as a recognizable clinical sign and pes planus representing common foot involvement.

## Disease Nomenclature and Literature Indexing

The condition is indexed in PubMed as Marfan syndrome [1][14][18], in MedGen as Marfan syndrome [2], and in literature entity databases as Marfan Syndrome [3].
